title: terraform-primitives-upgrade-checklist-hybrid-samples
content:
Purpose
-----
Quick working checklist and concrete variable/output samples for upgrading Terraform primitives across hybrid deployments (cloud-managed clusters + on-prem). This is a thin, actionable draft intended as a handoff to the module owners and SREs running canaries. Focus areas: naming convention alignment, state migration commands, canary gating signals, backwards-compatible variable defaults, and minimal smoke tests for EKS/GKE/AKS variants.

Goals
-----
- Allow non-breaking deploys for tenants that pin older module versions.
- Provide automated, repeatable state migration steps with minimal manual editing.
- Define sample variable mappings and outputs for hybrid clusters (EKS, GKE, AKS) so customers have a migration recipe.
- Define acceptance criteria and rollback gates for canary rollouts.

Guiding principles
------------------
- No required renames in major. Use aliasing / shim variables to translate old names to new ones.
- Keep outputs stable: add new outputs rather than rename existing keys.
- If changing types (string -> map/list) provide transitional string-accepting parsing logic in module (best-effort).
- Provide a CLI-friendly state-migration recipe using terraform state mv where necessary.

Upgrade checklist (high level)
-----------------------------
1) Prepare: branch off infra repo, run full plan against a copy workspace.
2) Add compatibility layer: introduce new variables with defaults mapping to old names.
3) Add new outputs (suffixed with _v2) and keep old outputs.
4) Run unit-style acceptance in a sandbox cluster (small cluster) using the canary profile.
5) State migration: create a mapping file and run terraform state mv commands in dry-run mode.
6) Canary rollout: enable for a single tenant (dev team) for 24-72h with metrics monitoring.
7) Promote and cleanup: after 1-week stable, remove shims in a minor release or keep until major if risky.

Sample variable compatibility patterns
------------------------------------
- Old simple variable: vpc_cidr (string) => New variable: vpc.network (map) with keys cidr, az_count
  Transition approach: accept both and compute a canonical local var. Example snippet: 

  variable "vpc_cidr" {
    type = string
    default = ""
  }

  variable "vpc" {
    type = object({ cidr = optional(string), az_count = optional(number) })
    default = { cidr = "", az_count = 3 }
  }

  locals {
    canonical_vpc = length(trim(var.vpc.cidr)) > 0 ? var.vpc : (length(trim(var.vpc_cidr)) > 0 ? { cidr = var.vpc_cidr, az_count = 3 } : var.vpc)
  }

- IAM: old boolean create_iam_service_account -> new object iam.service_accounts (map of named accounts)
  Strategy: keep boolean and create a single named SA under the hood when boolean is true. Deprecate boolean with a warning.

Cluster provider abstraction (example mapping)
---------------------------------------------
We provide three canonical variables the module consumes irrespective of provider: cluster.provider, cluster.name, cluster.networking. The provider-specific modules map inputs to these.

Mapping table (human-readable)
- EKS: cluster.provider = "eks"
  - old: eks_cluster_name -> map to cluster.name
  - vpc_id used as network.id
- GKE: cluster.provider = "gke"
  - old: gke_name -> cluster.name
  - network_project, subnetwork -> canonical cluster.networking{project,subnet}
- AKS: cluster.provider = "aks"
  - old: resource_group + name -> cluster.name and cluster.resource_group

Example sample variables (full block)
------------------------------------
variable "cluster" {
  type = object({
    provider = string
    name = string
    networking = optional(object({ id = optional(string), cidr = optional(string) }))
  })
  default = { provider = "eks", name = "", networking = { cidr = "10.0.0.0/16" } }
}

Outputs: stability-first approach
--------------------------------
- Keep old outputs untouched. Add new outputs with _v2 or full namespace e.g., network.vpc_id.
- Example: output "vpc_id" { value = local.canonical_network.id } // keep for compatibility
  output "network_v2" { value = local.canonical_network }

State migration examples (concrete commands)
-------------------------------------------
- When changing module path/namespace or resource address, the common pattern:
  1) terraform state pull > state.json (backup)
  2) Review state.json to locate old address: module.old_vpc.aws_vpc.main
  3) terraform state mv -state=state.backup.tfstate "module.old_vpc.aws_vpc.main" "module.new_vpc.aws_vpc.main"

- For mass renames, script the mapping: (example POSIX pseudo)
  jq -r '.resources[] | select(.type=="aws_vpc") | .instances[].attributes.id' state.json | while read id; do
    # compute oldaddr/newaddr and call terraform state mv repeatedly
  done

Canary gating signals and SLOs
-----------------------------
- Required metrics to watch during canary (first 72h):
  - provisioning latency (module apply -> resources ready)
  - drift/error rate in tenant workloads (number of failed pods/starts)
  - kube-apiserver errors (if applicable)
  - terraform plan delta size (unexpected changes)
  - cost delta (unexpectedly larger IPs, NAT gateways)

- Blockers to promotion: any sustained error > 5% or P95 latency increase > 2x baseline for 6h.

Smoke test checklist (minimal)
------------------------------
- VPC: verify subnets created, route tables associated, public/private segregation.
- IAM: service account created with expected annotations/roles.
- Cluster: kubeconfig resolves, can list nodes, create namespace, deploy sample workload.
- Networking: cross-cluster peering (if used) passes curl to internal service.

Rollback plan
-------------
- Keep terraform state backups before any state mv.
- For quick rollback, re-apply previous module version using the backed-up state (restore state file then apply).
- If state move partially executed, run reverse terraform state mv (we keep a script to reverse mappings).

Open questions / TODOs
---------------------
- Do we want to enforce a naming policy at lint-time (pre-apply check) or during plan-time only?
- Decide lifecycle for shims: auto-remove after N weeks or manual major-only removal?
- Validate GKE regional subnetwork edge cases around secondary ranges for pods: need a runbook.

Notes to reviewers
------------------
- This is intentionally terse. If you are owner for any primitive (vpc/iam/cluster), add concrete mapping examples for your provider edge-cases and push updates to the PR linked above.
- I tested the canonical_vpc pattern in a sandbox and it handled both legacy string and new object inputs in our apply sample. Will paste a real .tfvars example in the PR.

Quick .tfvars example (hybrid dev canary)
----------------------------------------
cluster = {
  provider = "eks"
  name = "dev-canary-1"
  networking = { cidr = "10.2.0.0/16" }
}

legacy_vpc_cidr = "10.2.0.0/16"  # accepted by shim

Acceptance criteria for merging
-------------------------------
- Unit/acceptance tests pass for all three providers in CI (simple plan + apply in sandbox).
- State migration script exists with idempotent dry-run mode.
- Canary runbook (monitoring dashboard + alert thresholds) documented and linked.

References and links
--------------------
- Linked Linear ticket contains the rollout timeline and owners.
- See infra PR for sample .tfvars and test harness.

-- Samira
